title: Warning Signs: Junctions, Bends & Layout
whatItIs: Signs that warn you about a hazard ahead, such as a junction, a bend or a change in the road layout. Most are triangles with a red border.
keyFacts: Most warning signs are triangles with a red border, a white background and a black symbol.
Circles give orders, triangles warn and rectangles mostly give information.
STOP (octagon) and GIVE WAY (upside-down triangle) break the shape rule so they stand out.
On junction signs, the broader line shows the road that has priority.
A plate below a sign adds to its message, for example the distance to the hazard.

visual.caption: Junction, bend and road layout warnings

a.label: Warning triangle (point up)
points: Tells you about a hazard ahead
Slow down and get ready to react

b.label: GIVE WAY (point down)
points: Let traffic on the major road go first

onTheTest.question: What shape are most warning signs?
onTheTest.why: Triangles warn, circles give orders and rectangles mostly inform. The octagon is used only for STOP.

onTheTest.question: On a crossroads warning sign, one line is broader than the other. What does the broader line show?
options: The road you must turn into
onTheTest.why: The broader line marks the priority route. If you're on the narrower road, expect to give way.

traps: Don't mix up the upside-down GIVE WAY triangle (an order) with warning triangles (a hazard ahead).
The triangular 'roundabout ahead' sign is a warning. The blue circle with three arrows is the mini-roundabout order.
Read the plate under the sign: it can tell you the distance to the hazard or how far it goes on.
